instructions: Drain the water chestnuts and chop them finely. Grate 2 tsp of the ginger and cut 2 thin slices from what's left. Mince 4 of the green onions and thinly slice the other 2 for the top.
Put the 1 lb pork in a large bowl, add 1/4 cup water and stir with a spatula until the water disappears into the meat.

Add the 1/4 cup Shaoxing wine, 3 tbsp of the soy sauce, the 1 tsp dark soy sauce, the 1 tsp salt, 2 tsp of the sugar, the grated ginger, 1 tbsp of the cornstarch and the minced green onions. Stir hard in one direction for a minute or two, until it turns sticky.

Stir in the water chestnuts and the 3 eggs, then the 1 cup panko, then the 2 tbsp sesame oil. It should be a soft paste that only just holds a shape. Soft is right, so the meatballs come out tender. If it slumps flat, stir in a spoonful more panko.

Cut the cabbage into 2-inch pieces and spread them in a wide Dutch oven or deep pot. Add the 4 cups broth, the last 1 tbsp soy sauce, the last 1/2 tsp sugar, the 1/4 tsp white pepper and the 2 ginger slices.

Heat the 3 tbsp oil in a large nonstick skillet over medium high until it shimmers, then turn it to medium. With wet hands, shape about 1/3 cup of the mixture into a loose ball and set it in the pan. Make 3 more, leaving room between them.

Cook until the underside is golden brown, 2 to 3 minutes. Roll each one gently with a spatula and brown another side for 2 to 3 minutes. Set them on top of the cabbage and brown the rest the same way. They'll still be raw in the middle.

Bring the pot to a boil over high heat, then cover it and turn it down so it simmers gently. Cook for 25 minutes, spooning broth over the meatballs halfway through. You're cooking them to 160°F in the middle, so if you have a thermometer, check one there. No thermometer? Cut one in half: it's done when there's no pink left.

Meanwhile, rinse the 1 1/2 cups jasmine rice in a sieve until the water runs mostly clear. Put it in a saucepan with 2 1/4 cups water and bring it to a boil over high heat. Cover, turn the heat to low and cook for 15 minutes, then take it off the heat and leave it covered for 10 minutes. No peeking.

Lift the meatballs onto a plate. Stir the last 1 tbsp cornstarch with 2 tbsp water until smooth. Bring the broth back to a boil, stir in the cornstarch mixture and simmer for 1 minute, until it thickens a little. Put the meatballs back in.
Taste the broth. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt.
Scatter the sliced green onions over the top and serve in bowls with the cabbage and broth, with the rice on the side.
method_notes: All three make a soft, wet mix of fatty ground pork with Shaoxing wine, soy, ginger, scallion and cornstarch, beaten until sticky, and brown big balls in oil before the long cook. Omnivore's Cookbook works water, egg, panko and chopped water chestnuts into the pork for a very tender ball, browns it in a skillet, then steams it for about 30 minutes. The Woks of Life deep-fries smaller balls and braises them in a soy and rock sugar sauce, and Melissa King's version (on EatDrinkFilms) fries them and simmers them on napa cabbage in seasoned chicken stock. This one uses Omnivore's Cookbook's mix and skillet browning, then braises the meatballs on napa cabbage the way Melissa King does, since the dish is the braised-with-cabbage kind.
